key_insight: eMOOD uses numerical entropy production to localise troubled cells, reducing flagged cells by up to 75% while preserving high-order shock-capturing accuracy and robustness.
engineering_relevance: The approach can accelerate compressible and multi-material flow simulations on unstructured meshes, with reported speed-ups of up to 20%.
method: Replace relaxed discrete maximum-principle detection with a compact entropy-production indicator.
Apply detection within a reduced-order MOOD cascade or a MOOD-CWENO hybrid that activates nonlinear reconstruction only where needed.
Implement and evaluate the method in the open-source parallel solver UCNS3D.
evidence_signal: Five benchmarks, including Shu–Osher interaction, double Mach reflection and shock–helium-bubble interaction, test shock capturing, instabilities and multi-material interfaces against reference CWENO and MOOD formulations.
watch_item: The reported gains are benchmark-dependent; the abstract does not establish performance across broader flow regimes or at massive parallel scale.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
